title: A phone dashboard that answers one question first
summary: I rebuilt my lab dashboard so each tab leads with what I can act on, and moved the pieces it needed into the UI kit. It is a remote I read on a phone, not a wall of counts.

stat.label: tabs, each opening on the answer: Now, Act, Services, Health and Work

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: My first dashboard showed four count tiles and several lists. It was accurate and I still could not tell, in one glance on a phone, whether anything needed me. A dashboard that makes me hunt is a report, not a remote.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: Now answers in one sentence: all clear, in green, or what needs me, in order. Act replaced the alerts and vulnerabilities tabs with one ranked list of items that each have a step: a service down on the side that serves, a down alert with no action card, exploited vulnerabilities, a late backup, then critical and high ones with a fix. Services keeps one switch card per service. Health shows backups and patches as signals, with trend charts that open on request. Work leads with items that wait on me.

Components that the dashboard drew by hand moved into the toonish-ui kit: a verdict, a readout that says what was read, a toggle with the right switch role, a masthead, and a two-button switch card. Version 0.4.0 added the uptime strip, line chart, status tile and switch row first. Green became the ok state colour, not a fifth accent. Each component writes its own roles and labels and carries a text equivalent, so unknown never reads as ok.

sections.heading: Staging that cannot change anything
paragraphs: I review on a phone, so the dashboard needs a staging copy. The staging host runs no branch code and holds no credential. It downloads a build published as a release asset, checks its SHA-256, and serves the files. It stays up for a set time after each publish.

The dashboard can read the lab's feed with my own sign-in cookie, from one allowed origin, so no token is stored anywhere. The staging copy has no switch endpoint to call, so it cannot move a service.

sections.heading: What went wrong
paragraphs: A code review of the rebuild found a case where Now could say all clear over a source it had not read. I fixed that: an unread source cannot produce an all clear. The same rule runs through the services list, where a missing lab reading shows as unknown. A demo mode uses a fixture, and a banner says the data is a demonstration.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: Each tab opens with its answer, and counts, charts and records sit under a row that opens. A poll keeps open rows open and focus where it was. I also wrote the reasoning down as a design-philosophy skill in the kit, including a rule that each page answers one question first, so the next screen starts from the same rules.

sections.heading: Lesson
paragraphs: Ask what question a screen answers before choosing its widgets. If the first thing on screen is not the answer, the screen is a report. And never let a view say all clear over data it did not read.
